metadata.original_title: 7 Healthy New Year 2024 Resolution Ideas for the LAZIEST
metadata.clean_title: 7 Healthy New Year 2024 Resolution Ideas for the LAZIEST
metadata.description:
New year 2024 is around the corner and it is time for resolutions. Every year, losing weight, eating healthy, and getting fit compete for our top resolutions. And by mid-January, the majority of those high-minded health goals have been abandoned, leaving us soured to the idea of positive change in the process. But it doesn't have to be this way. The problem is many healthy resolutions are too big and too vague to actually accomplish — so aim smaller and go specific. 

In support of the above, in this video I share with you 7 simple and healthy New Year resolutions that even the laziest of us can stick to.

Healthy New Year Resolution# 1 – Keep a water bottle handy, always. 

This is the bottle I use -  http://amzn.to/2hpfHko

Healthy New Year Resolution# 2 – Keep a healthy snack option with you.

Healthy New Year Resolution# 3 – Use an alternative to Sugar

Stevia Tablets -  http://amzn.to/2icLI0b
Stevia Sachets -  http://amzn.to/2i9Y2eZ

Healthy New Year Resolution# 4 – Use an alternative to Salt.

Rock Salt : http://amzn.to/2jskFdW
Black Salt : http://amzn.to/2hJvhor

Healthy New Year Resolution# 5 – Stop using electronic devices half an hour before you sleep.

Healthy New Year Resolution# 6 – Keep a hand sanitizer handy.

Hand Sanitizer : http://amzn.to/2iz4gYU

Healthy New Year Resolution# 7 – Try a new sport. 

Weren’t they simple?

Take a pick and let me know in the comments.

If you found this video helpful, do give it thumbs up. Share it with your friends.

SUBSCRIBE : https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCYC6Vcczj8v-Y5OgpEJTFBw

I wish you a very happy and healthy New Year 2017 :)

Fit Tuber

But, a genius will not just utilize it, but will also save his time and effort. He will often keep pulses and grains outside in the [00:01:20] sunlight, especially in the rainy season, to keep them free from any germs. In the winters, when washing is not so feasible, he will regularly place his blanket in the sunlight so that it remains fresh and warm. He will even [00:01:35] reap the benefits of sun-charged water. An ordinary person will crib about low vitamin D in his diet and might depend on synthetic tablets, whereas a genius will find time to sunbathe. He will expose his weakest body parts in the [00:01:51] sunlight because he knows that the sun is the ultimate doctor. An ignorant person will spray chemical deodorizers and disinfectants in his house, whereas a genius will keep the window shades open and allow nature's own sanitizer to [00:02:06] let in. He acknowledges how valuable sunlight is in reducing indoor pollution. A genius will make maximum use of mother nature's this divine gift because he knows that it naturally uplifts the mood, strengthens the immune [00:02:22] system, lowers the blood pressure, and improve sleep quality. Number four, a genius will eat local and seasonal food, no matter how nutritious it looks on paper, if it doesn't get absorbed by the body, it's not worth it, is it? An [00:02:38] ordinary person will fail to realize this. He will think that extensive is always better and will fall for off-season and sometimes even foreign fruits and vegetables at double prices from the supermarkets. A genius will smartly go to a local vegetable and [00:02:54] fruit vendor and buy the low-priced produce. That's because he knows that the fruits and vegetables which are the cheapest are seasonal. He understands that the items that are locally grown are to be more fresh and economical. And above all, he knows that the food which [00:03:10] is local and in season is not just tastier and juicier, but also gets better absorbed and assimilated in the body. While the genius is just paying for fruits and vegetables, an ignorant person is also paying for the cold storage and transportation. This is why [00:03:27] a genius will prefer coconut over avocado, cauliflower over broccoli, cabbage over lettuce, spinach over kale, red apples over green apples, and grapes over kiwis. What's tragic is that an ignorant man, even after spending so [00:03:42] much money on exotic foods, will face nutritional deficiencies. A genius will not just save money, his skin will be healthier, hair shinier, and body active. This will cost him health as well. A genius, on the other hand, will put just a little effort into making his home food as interesting as possible. First of all, he will focus on variety. He will frequently knead different vegetables in the chapati dough. He will eat different varieties of rice. He will experiment with different types of rice pulao. On some days, he will eat a besan ka [00:04:45] cheela, idli, dosa, millet biryani, or even multi-grain pancakes. He will keep rotating the lentils and beans. He will ensure that he eats a colorful variety of fruits and vegetables. He will also enjoy a variety of sweets prepared with [00:05:01] natural sweeteners because he realizes the value of sweet taste. He might design a meal plan and stick it in the kitchen so that he is well prepared. With just a little effort and planning, he won't just break the monotony of the same boring food, but with a variety of [00:05:18] foods, his diet will naturally encompass diverse micronutrients. Number two, a genius will not count calories. An ordinary person will try to break his fitness journey into the simple math of calorie counting. He will eat according to what the calculator tells him. He [00:05:35] will sign up with dieticians and simply note down how many calories he should eat, how much water he should drink, so on and so forth. A genius, on the other hand, will remain wary of the fact that not all calories are the same. 200 calories from a soft drink will not [00:05:50] provide him as much nourishment as 200 calories from fresh milk. He knows that cutting down on good calories deprives the body of energy and key vitamins and minerals. Instead of getting into the fuss of counting calories, he will eat his food mindfully, relishing every bit [00:06:08] of it. Instead of paying a hefty fee to the dieticians, he will tune into his very own dietician, the stomach. If on a certain day he feels full, he might skip his dinner. On a certain day if he is feeling very hungry, he might eat accordingly. He will be able to [00:06:24] determine if he is really hungry or just thirsty. And guess who loses more weight? Of course, a genius. Even Harvard Medical School agrees that this idea of a calorie in and a calorie out when it comes to weight loss is not only [00:06:39] outdated, it's just wrong. So, listen to your body and thrive like a genius. Finally, at number one, a genius will eat smartly. Overeating even the healthiest foods is a sure shot way to health problems. Firstly, an ordinary person will overeat just to avoid [00:06:56] wastage of food. If he is unable to finish it anyway, he will keep the food stored in a refrigerator, which he will later reheat and eat. A genius appreciates the fact that food is most beneficial for the body when consumed fresh and in the right quantity. A [00:07:12] genius will foremost try to prepare only a sufficient quantity of food. If, however, the prepared food is extra, he will surely not overeat and overload his body. He will not even refrigerate, reheat, and consume the same food as he is conscious enough that food has living [00:07:29] prana, which gets reduced with time. Since he believes that food wastage is a human-centric idea, he will instead share it with animals and other creatures around him. Instead of making a dreadful experience for his body, he is thoughtful enough to make it a [00:07:44] pleasant experience for other life forms around him. And not to forget the mental satisfaction that he will get by this responsible act of kindness.
